post.linkedin_text:
AI won't run your marketing for you. But it can take a lot of the slow work off your plate.

I think a lot of small business owners either ignore AI completely or expect it to do everything. Actually, the useful part is somewhere in the middle.

So here's how I'd explain it, simply.

Where AI helps today:

1. First drafts of captions. Give it your offer and your audience, and you get a few options to start from. Much faster than staring at a blank screen.

2. Research. Ask it what questions customers usually have about your kind of business. That gives you content ideas for the month.

3. Ad targeting ideas. It can suggest audience angles to test, like interests, age groups or different reasons people buy.

4. Repurposing. One long video or blog can be turned into short post ideas.

Where a human still matters:

→ Knowing your customers. AI doesn't know that your regulars come in after 7 pm or what they always ask at the counter.
→ Taste. Deciding what actually looks and sounds like your brand.
→ The shoot itself. Someone still has to show up, frame the shot and capture the real place.
→ Judgement. Checking every fact before it goes out, because AI can get things wrong with full confidence.

So the simple way to think about it: let AI do the first draft and the research. Keep the decisions and the final call with people who know your business.

This is how we use it at Loyara too.
